newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian airports to invest $2.9 bln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian airports to invest $2.9 bln by 2000.

text.p: Brazil's national airport administration Infraero said it will invest $2.9 billion in the next four years to modernize and expand major Brazilian airports.
Under the plan, Infraero will start the construction of a third passenger terminal in South America's largest airport Cumbica, located in Guarulhos in Sao Paulo state, said a Infraero spokeswoman.
Infraero also will expand Cumbica's two other passenger terminals, she said.

Among other Brazilian airports which will expand or build passenger terminals in 1997 are Florianopolis, Pelotas, Maceio, Belo Horizonte, Uberaba, Uberlandia, Londrina, Campo Grande and Porto Velho, she added.
She said new cargo terminals in Curitiba, Cumbica, Viracopos, Recife and Manaus airports would begin operating in 1997.

Last year, 50.2 million people flew through Brazilian airports, a rise of 8.5 percent over 1995, Infraero reported. Cargo moving through Brazilian airports rose 7.2 percent reaching 1.2 million tonnes last year, it said.
